title: Hollow Elm
contentNote: Contains horror themes, tense chase sequences and flashing lights. Settings include a reduced-flash option.

chapters.title: 02:03 — Unknown Number
chapters.objective: Read your messages. Decide whether to tell Dale. Follow the photograph to Alder Hollow.
chapters.intro: Three weeks since Juniper Hale vanished. You stopped answering the precinct. Tonight, someone has found your number.
chapters.inWorldHint: The photograph shows an elm over the gate and a market label on a jar.
chapters.phoneHint: Priya recognizes the jam label. Ask Dale about Juniper's last location, then choose whether to share the message.

chapters.title: The Jam Lady
chapters.objective: Find the pantry key, enter the study, photograph the ledger, and search the living-room clock. Reach the barn.
chapters.intro: The scullery window opens under your hand. A kettle whistles somewhere inside. Then a small voice: 'Oh, you're lost, dear. Sit. I'll put the kettle on.' The window latch falls shut.
chapters.inWorldHint: A kitchen note reads: 'Pantry key by the jars. Study spare inside. When the clock stops at two, turn its little heart.'
chapters.phoneHint: Check the kitchen jars for the pantry key. The pantry holds the study key. Photograph the open ledger with your flashlight on, then inspect the clock in the living room.

chapters.title: The House Rearranges
chapters.objective: Take the bathroom fuse to the attic record player. Play the tape, collect the music-box key, and photograph the nursery page.
chapters.intro: You wake in the barn to the same lullaby. The hall cabinet has moved. Tins hang in the doorway you used last night. The phone glows: 'She keeps the tape upstairs.'
chapters.inWorldHint: A faded repair tag says: 'Bathroom cupboard — spare fuse. Player powers the recorder. Wind the little box before the last verse.'
chapters.phoneHint: The bathroom cupboard holds a fuse. Repair the record player in the attic to power the tape recorder. Its compartment contains a music-box key. The nursery page matters.

chapters.title: The Cellar
chapters.objective: Find two batteries. Connect the ledger to the nursery page for the shelf code. Open the hidden door and reach Juniper.
chapters.intro: The cellar smells of apples and wet earth. Behind the preserves, someone taps twice. Then once. Mother Marrow has stopped humming.
chapters.inWorldHint: The shelf dial bears the words 'First arrival / last return.' The ledger dates and torn nursery page complete the numbers. A crowbar lies beside the coal crates.
chapters.phoneHint: Link the ledger and nursery page on the evidence board to reveal 0219. Use the crowbar after entering the shelf code. The music-box key opens the inner room. Carry a spare battery.

chapters.title: The Elm Wood
chapters.objective: Silence the phone. Lead Juniper and her sister through the garden to the road. Decide whose messages you believe.
chapters.intro: Beyond the garden, the first pale strip of dawn catches the elm trunks. Juniper keeps looking back. Her sister holds the hem of her coat. Behind you, a cane strikes the stones.
chapters.inWorldHint: The garden map marks a drainage path to the road. A warning on its back reads: 'The lantern route circles home.'
chapters.phoneHint: Keep the phone on vibrate. Follow the drainage path. Messages mentioning the lantern or the kettle repeat Marrow's ledger language; Juniper's true warnings refer to her sister and the clock.

messages.text: I'm still here. Don't call anyone. [Photo: a farmhouse beneath an elm.]

choices.text: Juniper? Where are you?
Who gave you my number?
choices.response: You were the only one who kept looking.

messages.text: Mara. Please stop going through that case. The last confirmed sighting was the Alder Hollow market. Juniper left on foot toward Briar Lane. That's all we have.

choices.text: She sent me a farmhouse photo. I'm going there.
choices.response: Send the address. I can't pull a team on a text, but I will check on you. Don't make me find your phone in a ditch.

choices.text: I'm just checking an old lead.
choices.response: You always say 'just.' Call if something changes.

messages.text: Juniper talked to the lady who sells jam. Marrow. She said the woman knew where her sister was. I thought she meant an address. I should have asked.

choices.text: What did Juniper say before leaving?
choices.response: 'If she asks, say I came alone.' I didn't understand. The jam label says Hollow Elm preserves.

choices.text: Why didn't you tell the police?
choices.response: They called her a runaway before I finished speaking. I got scared. I'm still scared.

messages.text: Are you there? Mara? Please answer. [Your notification rings across the kitchen.]

choices.text: I need to be quiet.
choices.response: Then silence your phone. I'll keep typing. You don't have to reply.

choices.text: She's inside.

messages.text: She keeps the tape upstairs. Stay by the lantern. The kettle will tell you when it's safe.

choices.text: Why the lantern?
choices.response: So she can see you're not lost.

choices.text: You sound different.

messages.text: Not the lantern. Clock stopped at two. My sister came on the nineteenth. Please remember. Delete this if she asks.

choices.text: I remember.
choices.response: There is a shelf downstairs that doesn't touch the wall.

choices.text: Did you bring other people here?
choices.response: I thought she'd let my sister go. She never did.

messages.text: I'm at the gate. Chain's new. I can hear someone humming. Tell me which window.

choices.text: Stay outside. Meet us at the drainage path by the road.
choices.response: Understood. I'll get the gate covered. Bring them out, Mara.

choices.text: Come through the scullery. I need help.
choices.response: Moving now. Keep your light on so I can find you.

messages.text: The road is blocked. Bring Juniper back to the lantern. I'll put the kettle on.

choices.text: That isn't Juniper.
We're coming back.
choices.response: Good. Nobody has to be lonely.

evidence.title: The ledger of arrivals
evidence.description: Names, market dates, and a repeated phrase: 'A place at the table.' Juniper's entry: 02. Her sister's arrival day is obscured by a torn corner. Photograph the ledger.

evidence.title: Market receipt
evidence.description: Hollow Elm preserves, paid in cash. On the reverse: 'Juniper — ask for your sister, not the police.' The handwriting matches the lantern instructions.

evidence.title: Stopped clock photograph
evidence.description: Both hands at two. Scratched inside its door: 'J. If I say clock, it is me.' A small key rests beneath the pendulum.

evidence.title: Torn nursery page
evidence.description: An adult sister's note: 'I arrived on the 19th. She wrote my day after Juniper's number. First arrival, last return. Four digits.'

evidence.title: The attic recording
evidence.description: Juniper asks how many people she must bring before her sister can leave. Marrow answers, 'A family isn't counted. It is kept.' The recorder clicks; Juniper whispers, 'Don't follow her lantern.'

evidence.title: Unsent letters
evidence.description: Letters from the people Marrow 'kept.' Each ends with a plea to be allowed home. Her marginal note repeats: 'The kettle will tell you when it is safe.'

evidence.title: Drainage route
evidence.description: A gardener's map leads from the garden culvert to the road. The lantern trail doubles back to the house. A pencilled J marks the safe turn.

evidence.title: Two blankets
evidence.description: Two sleeping places, two names on the wall: Juniper and Rowan Hale. Rowan is alive. A scratched line reads: 'She made June send the messages. Please don't leave her.'

deductions.title: First arrival, last return
deductions.text: Juniper's ledger number is 02. Her sister arrived on the 19th. Together they open the preserves shelf: 0219.

deductions.title: Two voices on one phone
deductions.text: Clock messages use Juniper's private marker. Kettle and lantern messages repeat Marrow's phrases. One phone carries two voices.

deductions.title: Bait under coercion
deductions.text: Juniper lured people to protect Rowan. She did harm, but Marrow controlled the bargain. There is still time to bring both sisters out.

deductions.title: The route that returns
deductions.text: The market instructions and lantern path lead back into Marrow's control. The drainage route reaches the road.

patrol: A little kindness keeps the cold away.
investigate: I hear you, dear. I hear everything.
Floorboards talk. They always tell me.
search: Come out, the tea's getting cold.
chase: You cannot carry loneliness into the wood.
I kept a place for you.

tape.speaker: Juniper
tape.text: You said one more visitor. You promised Rowan could go.

tape.speaker: Mother Marrow
tape.text: Promises change when a family grows, dear. You brought me people nobody would miss.

tape.speaker: Juniper
tape.text: Someone misses every one of them.

tape.speaker: Mother Marrow
tape.text: Then they should have come sooner. Read the message again. Tell her not to call anyone.

tape.speaker: Juniper, whispering
tape.text: Mara, if you hear this: the clock means it's me. The lantern means she's watching. Rowan is behind the shelves. Don't leave her.

choices.text: The clock messages. The kettle was Marrow speaking through you.
The lantern. It told us where we belonged.
I don't know. Keep moving.

finalPrompts.prompt: Juniper: 'I brought them here. I thought she would let Rowan go.'

choices.text: The tape proves she coerced you. Both of you come with me.
Rowan comes with me. You need to face what you did.
We can't go back. Come now, Juniper.

finalPrompts.prompt: Juniper: 'The lantern trail or the ditch? Tell me now.'

choices.text: The drainage path reaches the road. Keep the phone silent.
The ditch. Stay beside me. We'll answer for everything in daylight.
The new message says the road is blocked. Follow the lantern.

dawn.title: Dawn
dawn.text: You bring both sisters to the road. Dale is safe beyond the gate. The ledger, recording, and photographs hold together in the morning light. Mother Marrow is arrested before the kettle boils. Juniper's testimony begins with the names she was told nobody remembered.

hollow.title: Hollow
hollow.text: One sister reaches the road with you. Behind the elm trees, a lantern goes dark. Search teams find the cellar open and the house empty. The case stays on your desk. This time, nobody calls it a runaway.

guest.title: Marrow's Guest
guest.text: A phone lights the study. Your name is the newest line in the ledger. Beyond the locked door, a kettle whistles. An unknown number sends a photograph of the farmhouse: 'I'm still here. Don't call anyone.'
